items.title: Your Agent Stack Is Broken at the Bottom
items.reason: Directly relevant to Priya’s production-agent work: it focuses on the real-time data layer, concurrency, scale, and cost bottlenecks that can make autonomous agents fail in practice.
items.question: When agent workloads shift from human-speed queries to machine-speed concurrency, which data-layer SLOs do you recommend teams monitor first to catch reliability regressions before users do?

items.title: How to Govern AI even If It's Hard to Predict
items.reason: Matches Priya’s interest in safe, governed production LLM systems by showing how model routing and orchestration can enforce cost, data-location, and vendor-risk policies without freezing delivery.
items.question: In Kimchi’s five-role multi-model routing architecture, how do you test that routing policies continue to enforce governance goals when model capabilities or prices change underneath the system?

items.title: Running AI Agents Safely on Production Systems
items.reason: A high-signal fit for agent security and production autonomy: it covers how D. E. Shaw lets agents write code, execute it, and act on live systems inside controlled safety boundaries.
items.question: What is the most useful boundary between autonomy and control that you have found for agents acting on live systems: permission scopes, sandboxing, human approval gates, or post-action rollback?

items.title: Lunch
Explainability is an infrastructure problem, not a model problem
items.reason: Especially relevant to fintech: it reframes explainability as decision-time data retention and architecture, not just SHAP/LIME/model-card artifacts after the fact.
items.question: For regulated credit or fraud decisions, what minimum evidence should be captured at inference time so that a single decision remains explainable six weeks later after features and models have changed?

items.title: Stop counting tokens. Start measuring outcomes.
items.reason: Hits Priya’s cost-and-economics priority by moving beyond token price to cost per successful business outcome, including caching, idle capacity, data movement, tooling, and ops overhead.
items.question: In the insurance-renewal example, which hidden cost component most often changes the architecture choice once you measure cost per successful outcome rather than cost per token?

items.title: Agent Harness for Enterprise: Engineering the Runtime for Reliable AI Agents
items.reason: This must-attend workshop is the centerpiece for Priya: it covers runtime patterns for skill discovery, context compaction, tool execution, verification loops, identity propagation, observability, governance, and reliable enterprise-scale agents.
items.question: When designing an Agent Harness, which verification loop gives the best reliability lift per unit of latency: tool-result validation, plan review, execution checkpoints, or post-task audit?

items.title: The Agentic Platform: Powering Operations for Real Business Outcomes
items.reason: Gives Priya an enterprise-platform view of orchestration, context, integration, governance, and measurable outcomes—the connective tissue needed to ship agents beyond pilots.
items.question: What platform capability should teams standardize first when moving from isolated agent pilots to responsible, reusable agentic operations: context management, governance, integrations, or observability?

items.title: Lunch
Beyond Agents: Building Systems of Enterprise Intelligence
items.reason: Strong fit for agentic orchestration at scale: it addresses coordination across agents, workflows, data, people, economics, and the ‘Intelligence Yield’ of AI consumption.
items.question: How do you quantify the Coordination Tax of fragmented agents in a way engineering and business teams can both act on?

items.title: This House Believes AI Will Give India Its Biggest Economic Opportunity in a Generation
items.reason: Satisfies the panel/debate requirement while giving Priya a broader lens on AI economics, productivity, jobs, and India’s competitive advantage—useful context for fintech product strategy.
items.question: For India’s AI opportunity to become broad-based rather than skill-biased, what technical or policy lever would most directly reduce the gap between AI producers and AI users?

items.title: Operations + AI: Beyond Automation: Reimagining Supply Chains, Manufacturing and Operations with AI
items.reason: Useful for translating agentic systems into operational outcomes: it focuses on integrated AI operating models that sense, predict, decide, adapt, and scale beyond pilots.
items.question: When moving from isolated AI use cases to an integrated operating model, which bottleneck usually blocks scale first: data foundations, process redesign, team adoption, or outcome measurement?

items.title: Agentic Data Cloud: From building the analytics data foundation with Knowledge Catalog, federating it with transactional data to generating advanced insights using Agentic Intelligence.
items.reason: Adds a second hands-on workshop and reinforces Priya’s production concerns around data foundations, catalogs, federation, and data agents for advanced insights.
items.question: In a federated data-agent setup, how do you prevent the agent from producing confident insights when catalog metadata is incomplete, stale, or inconsistent across transactional systems?

items.title: Token Tax Saver Schemes: 7 Design Choice Hacks
items.reason: Direct match for Priya’s cost focus: it treats token efficiency as an upfront design problem and promises production-tested levers across architecture, model selection, human-agent co-delivery, and controls.
items.question: Of the seven design hacks, which one typically reduces token spend without increasing operational complexity or harming task-success rate?

items.title: The Best Model Is Not the Biggest Model: Engineering the Economics of Enterprise AI
items.reason: Excellent fit for Priya’s small-vs-big-model economics interest: it covers routing, SLMs, prompt optimization, agentic architectures, and reserving larger models only where needed.
items.question: What evaluation threshold should trigger routing from a small model to a larger model: confidence, task class, expected business risk, or measured failure cost?

items.title: Crash. Resume. Repeat: Building Agents That Don't Die
items.reason: Directly targets agent reliability in production by demonstrating durable execution, retries, state preservation, and recovery when an agent dies mid-task.
items.question: How do you design idempotency and checkpoint granularity so a resumed agent neither repeats side effects nor skips necessary recovery work?

items.title: The Agent Economy: Who owns the customer when the agent is the interface?
items.reason: Highly relevant to fintech strategy: it probes ownership, transactions, agent intermediaries, and the banking equivalent of an agent choosing products or payment rails for users.
items.question: If an agent chooses a credit card or financial product for a customer, what should determine accountability: the user mandate, the agent platform, the issuing institution, or the merchant network?

items.title: Lunch
The Trust Deficit: Building Responsible AI in a Regulated, Risk-Heavy Business
items.reason: A strong fintech-specific pick on responsible AI, governance, explainability, bias mitigation, model oversight, and human accountability in regulated financial services.
items.question: What is one responsible-AI control that looks optional in early pilots but becomes non-negotiable once AI affects credit, fraud, compliance, or customer outcomes at scale?

items.title: The Scaling Loop: The Secret Relationship Between Small and Big Models
items.reason: Complements the enterprise-AI economics sessions by exploring frugally scalable AI and what building foundation models at multiple scales teaches about when constraint can improve model design.
items.question: What did BharatGen learn at smaller scales that changed decisions for larger-scale models, and how can application teams use that lesson when choosing between SLMs and frontier models?

summary: Priya’s Cypher 2026 plan is optimized for production GenAI engineering: agent runtime reliability, safe production autonomy, governance, explainability for regulated contexts, token and model economics, and agentic systems at enterprise scale. It avoids her prior SDLC/vibe-coding, RAG, and voice-AI topics, respects all commitments and hall-transition buffers, includes lunch each day, includes two workshops, and balances 6, 5, and 6 non-lunch sessions across the three days.
